page: Microsoft Azure F1alds_v7 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the Faldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory and 118 GB of local storage, with support for Premium Storage.

The AMD EPYC processor features 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores placing in the top 10%. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%.

Memory performance is mixed; the Passmark memory score is in the bottom 10%, and small-block cached read bandwidth is in the bottom 25%, though large-block read and write bandwidths reach average tiers. The server lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not include a GPU. Given the low memory capacity of 2.0 GB and weak multi-core throughput, this instance is suited for single-threaded utility tasks, lightweight background workers, or basic web serving where high single-core efficiency is required but memory and multi-threaded scaling are not critical.
